description: An average hides the story. Two teams can both close tickets in 20 days on average while one is predictable and the other swings between 2 and 90. A bar chart of averages shows them as equal; the people waiting on the second team know they are not. Box & Whisker by TCViz shows how the values of each category are spread: the median, the middle half of the values, how far the normal range reaches and which cases fall outside it. Power BI has no built-in box plot; this one reads at a glance and says exactly how it counts. READ IT AT A GLANCE • One box per category: median, first and third quartile, whiskers and outliers • n under every box, so a box built on 12 rows is not mistaken for one built on 12,000 • Whiskers at 1.5 × IQR (Tukey) or minimum to maximum • Quartiles with the inclusive method, the same as Excel QUARTILE.INC; the method is named in every tooltip • Vertical or horizontal; six style templates, including an IBCS style PRO • Group: boxes side by side inside each category, with a legend • Small multiples on a shared scale, with columns, titles and panel styles • All points with jitter, mean marker, notches (approximate 95% interval of the median) and a violin behind each box • Colour by quartile; sort by median, mean, IQR or count • Exclusive quartiles (Excel QUARTILE.EXC) and Tukey hinges; whiskers at the 5th–95th or 10th–90th percentile • Two reference lines and a…
